title: Gold affine equivalence of the Gamma-zero quadrinomials
summary: Determine whether every admissible Gamma-zero permutation quadrinomial is affine equivalent to the corresponding Gold permutation; this is known for the closed-butterfly subfamily only.

formal_statement.body: Let $m$ and $k$ be odd with $\gcd(m,k)=1$, and let $f_{\mathbf c}$ be the source-defined permutation quadrinomial over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$ for an admissible coefficient tuple $\mathbf c\in\Gamma_0$. Is every such $f_{\mathbf c}$ affine equivalent to the Gold permutation $$x\longmapsto x^{2^k+1}?$$ Prove the equivalence for all of $\Gamma_0$, or exhibit an admissible counterexample. The closed-butterfly parameterized subfamily is already known to be linearly equivalent to Gold.

scope.domain: The full source-defined Gamma-zero family of permutation quadrinomials over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$
assumptions: $f_{\mathbf c}$ is the source-defined permutation quadrinomial
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove Gold affine equivalence for every admissible Gamma-zero coefficient tuple not covered by the closed-butterfly parameterization, or exhibit and classify a counterexample.

progress.summary: The source asks whether every member of the full four-coefficient Gamma-zero family is affine equivalent to the corresponding Gold permutation.
Li, Hu, Xiong, and Zeng prove linear equivalence to Gold for the strict closed-butterfly parameterized subfamily, leaving general Gamma-zero coefficients open.
